articles.title: My Family
articles.text: I have a small family. There are four people in my family. They are my father, my mother, my sister and me. My father is a teacher. My mother is a doctor. My sister is a student. I am a student too. We love each other. We are happy.
articles.textCn: 我有一个小家庭。我家有四口人。他们是我爸爸、我妈妈、我姐姐和我。我爸爸是老师。我妈妈是医生。我姐姐是学生。我也是学生。我们彼此相爱。我们很幸福。

quiz.q: How many people are in the family?

comprehension.q: How does the writer feel about the family?
What can we guess about the family?
options: They do not love each other
They live together and love each other

articles.title: My Day
articles.text: I get up at seven in the morning. I wash my face and brush my teeth. I eat breakfast at half past seven. I go to school at eight. I have lunch at school. I come home at four in the afternoon. I do my homework. I go to bed at nine.
articles.textCn: 我早上七点起床。我洗脸刷牙。我七点半吃早饭。我八点去上学。我在学校吃午饭。我下午四点回家。我做作业。我九点上床睡觉。

Where does the writer have lunch?
What time does the writer go to bed?
What does the writer do after coming home?

comprehension.q: What kind of person is the writer?

articles.title: My Friend
articles.text: I have a good friend. His name is Tom. He is tall and strong. He has short black hair and big eyes. He likes sports. He plays football every day. He is good at math. He often helps me with my math. We are good friends.
articles.textCn: 我有一个好朋友。他的名字叫汤姆。他又高又壮。他有黑色的短发和大大的眼睛。他喜欢运动。他每天踢足球。他擅长数学。他经常帮我学数学。我们是好朋友。

quiz.q: What subject is Tom good at?

comprehension.q: What can we guess about Tom?
options: He does not like the writer

articles.title: My School
articles.text: My school is big and beautiful. There are many trees and flowers in it. We have a library, a playground and twenty classrooms. There are fifty teachers and eight hundred students. I love my school. I learn many new things every day. I play with my friends at school.
articles.textCn: 我的学校又大又漂亮。里面有许多树和花。我们有一个图书馆、一个操场和二十间教室。有五十名老师和八百名学生。我爱我的学校。我每天学到许多新东西。我在学校和朋友一起玩。

quiz.q: What does the writer do at school?

comprehension.q: How does the writer feel about the school?

articles.title: My Pet
articles.text: I have a pet cat. Her name is Mimi. She is white and small. She has two big green eyes. She likes to eat fish. She likes to play with a ball. She sleeps on my bed every night. I love Mimi. She is my best friend.
articles.textCn: 我有一只宠物猫。她的名字叫咪咪。她又白又小。她有两只绿色的大眼睛。她喜欢吃鱼。她喜欢玩球。她每天晚上睡在我的床上。我爱咪咪。她是我最好的朋友。

articles.title: My Room
articles.text: My room is small but clean. There is a bed, a desk and a chair in it. The bed is next to the window. The desk is near the door. I have many books on the desk. I have a lamp on the desk too. There is a picture of my family on the wall. I like my room very much. I read and do my homework there every day.
articles.textCn: 我的房间很小但很干净。里面有一张床、一张书桌和一把椅子。床在窗户旁边。书桌在门附近。我书桌上有许多书。书桌上也有一盏台灯。墙上有一张我家人的照片。我非常喜欢我的房间。我每天都在那里看书和做作业。

comprehension.q: What can we guess about the writer?
options: He never stays in his room

articles.title: My Favorite Food
articles.text: My favorite food is noodles. I eat noodles every week. My mother makes noodles for me. She puts eggs and vegetables in them. They are very delicious. Sometimes I eat noodles at a restaurant with my father. I like noodles best. I can eat a big bowl. I am happy when I eat noodles.
articles.textCn: 我最喜欢的食物是面条。我每周都吃面条。我妈妈给我做面条。她在面条里放鸡蛋和蔬菜。它们非常美味。有时我和爸爸在餐馆吃面条。我最喜欢面条。我能吃一大碗。吃面条时我很开心。

articles.title: My Weekend
articles.text: I love weekends. On Saturday, I play with my friends. We go to the park and fly kites. In the evening, I watch TV with my family. On Sunday, I help my mother at home. I clean the room and water the flowers. Then I do my homework. Weekend is short but happy. I look forward to it every week.
articles.textCn: 我喜欢周末。星期六，我和朋友一起玩。我们去公园放风筝。晚上，我和家人一起看电视。星期天，我在家帮妈妈。我打扫房间、浇花。然后我做作业。周末短暂但快乐。我每周都期待着它。

What does the writer do on Sunday?

articles.title: My Teacher
articles.text: My English teacher is Miss Wang. She is tall and has long hair. She is kind and patient. She always smiles at us. She teaches us English songs and games. We learn a lot in her class. When we make mistakes, she does not get angry. She helps us try again. All the students like her very much.
articles.textCn: 我的英语老师是王老师。她个子很高，留着长发。她善良又耐心。她总是对我们微笑。她教我们英语歌曲和游戏。我们在她的课上学到很多。当我们犯错时，她不生气。她帮助我们再试一次。所有的学生都非常喜欢她。

comprehension.q: Why do the students like Miss Wang?

articles.title: My Hobby
articles.text: My hobby is drawing. I like drawing pictures of animals. I draw cats, dogs, birds and fish. I draw every day after school. I have many colors of pencils. My mother buys them for me. I put my pictures on the wall. My friends say my pictures are beautiful. Drawing makes me happy. I want to be an artist when I grow up.
articles.textCn: 我的爱好是画画。我喜欢画动物的画。我画猫、狗、鸟和鱼。我每天放学后画画。我有许多颜色的铅笔。妈妈给我买的。我把画贴在墙上。朋友们说我的画很漂亮。画画让我开心。我长大后想当一名艺术家。

quiz.q: What does the writer want to be?

comprehension.q: What can we guess about the writer?
options: He is not good at drawing

articles.title: A Trip to the Park
articles.text: Last Sunday, my family went to the park. The weather was sunny and warm. We arrived there at nine in the morning. The park was full of people. Some children were flying kites. Some old people were dancing under the trees. My parents sat on the grass and talked. My little brother played with a ball. I rode my bicycle around the lake. At noon, we had a picnic under a big tree. My mother made sandwiches and my father brought fruit juice. After lunch, we took many photos. We left the park at four in the afternoon. We were tired but very happy. It was a wonderful day.
articles.textCn: 上周日，我们一家去了公园。天气晴朗又温暖。我们早上九点到达那里。公园里到处是人。一些孩子在放风筝。一些老人在树下跳舞。我的父母坐在草地上聊天。我的小弟弟在玩球。我绕着湖骑自行车。中午，我们在一棵大树下野餐。妈妈做了三明治，爸爸带了果汁。午饭后，我们拍了很多照片。我们下午四点离开公园。我们很累但是很开心。这是美好的一天。

articles.title: My Weekend
articles.text: I love weekends because I can relax. On Saturday morning, I usually sleep late. After breakfast, I do my homework. In the afternoon, I often go shopping with my mother. We buy vegetables, fruit and some snacks. Sometimes we watch a movie at the cinema. On Sunday, I visit my grandparents. They live in a small town near the city. My grandmother cooks delicious food for us. My grandfather tells me interesting stories about his past. In the evening, I come back home and pack my schoolbag for Monday. Weekend is short but happy. I always look forward to it.
articles.textCn: 我喜欢周末因为我可以放松。星期六早上，我通常睡到很晚。早饭后，我做作业。下午，我经常和妈妈去购物。我们买蔬菜、水果和一些零食。有时我们在电影院看电影。星期天，我去看望爷爷奶奶。他们住在城市附近的一个小镇上。奶奶给我们做美味的食物。爷爷给我讲他过去的有趣故事。晚上，我回到家，为星期一收拾书包。周末短暂但快乐。我一直期待着它。

articles.title: Shopping Day
articles.text: Today is Saturday. My mother and I went shopping in the city center. We took a bus to get there. First, we went to a clothes shop. I bought a blue T-shirt and a pair of black shoes. My mother bought a red dress. Then we went to a bookshop. I bought two storybooks. After that, we went to a supermarket. We bought some milk, bread, eggs and apples. We were hungry, so we had lunch at a small restaurant. I had noodles and my mother had rice with chicken. We carried many bags home. We spent a lot of money, but we were very happy.
articles.textCn: 今天是星期六。我和妈妈去市中心购物。我们坐公交车去那里。首先，我们去了服装店。我买了一件蓝色T恤和一双黑鞋。妈妈买了一条红色连衣裙。然后我们去了书店。我买了两本故事书。之后，我们去了一家超市。我们买了一些牛奶、面包、鸡蛋和苹果。我们饿了，所以我们在一家小餐馆吃了午饭。我吃了面条，妈妈吃了鸡肉饭。我们提着很多袋子回家。我们花了不少钱，但是我们很开心。

articles.title: A Birthday Party
articles.text: Yesterday was my birthday. I had a party at home. I invited ten friends. The party started at six in the evening. My mother made a big chocolate cake. My father bought some juice, fruit and snacks. My friends brought me many presents. There were books, toys and cards. We sang the birthday song together. I made a wish and blew out the candles. Then we ate the cake and other food. After that, we played games. We played hide-and-seek and told funny stories. Everyone laughed a lot. The party ended at nine in the evening. My friends went home. It was the best birthday ever.
articles.textCn: 昨天是我的生日。我在家办了一个派对。我邀请了十个朋友。派对晚上六点开始。妈妈做了一个大巧克力蛋糕。爸爸买了一些果汁、水果和零食。朋友们给我带了很多礼物。有书、玩具和卡片。我们一起唱了生日歌。我许了一个愿望，吹灭了蜡烛。然后我们吃蛋糕和其他食物。之后，我们玩游戏。我们玩了捉迷藏，讲了有趣的故事。大家都笑得很开心。派对晚上九点结束。朋友们回家了。这是有史以来最好的生日。

articles.title: My Hometown
articles.text: My hometown is a small village in the south. It is not big, but it is very beautiful. There are green hills around it. A small river runs through the village. The water is clean and there are fish in it. There are about two hundred families in our village. People here are friendly and kind. Most of them are farmers. They grow rice and vegetables. In spring, the fields are full of green plants. In autumn, people are busy with the harvest. The air in my hometown is fresh. The sky is blue. There are many trees and flowers. I love my hometown very much. When I grow up, I want to make it more beautiful.
articles.textCn: 我的家乡是南方的一个小村庄。它不大，但是非常美丽。它的周围有青山。一条小河穿过村庄。水很干净，里面有鱼。我们村大约有两百户人家。这里的人们友好善良。他们大多数是农民。他们种水稻和蔬菜。春天，田野里满是绿色植物。秋天，人们忙着收割。我家乡的空气清新。天空蔚蓝。有很多树和花。我非常爱我的家乡。长大后，我想把它变得更美丽。

articles.title: At the Library
articles.text: I love going to the library. It is my favorite place in the city. The library is big and quiet. There are thousands of books on many shelves. You can find storybooks, history books, science books and magazines there. Every Saturday, I go to the library with my friend Lily. We both love reading. We usually stay there for two hours. First, we find books we like. Then we sit by the window and read. The librarians are kind and helpful. They help us find the books we need. We must keep quiet in the library. We cannot eat or run there. Before we leave, we borrow two books each. We can keep them for two weeks. Then we must return them. Reading makes me happy and smart. I want to read every book in the library.
articles.textCn: 我喜欢去图书馆。它是我在这个城市最喜欢的地方。图书馆又大又安静。许多书架上有成千上万本书。你可以在那里找到故事书、历史书、科学书和杂志。每个星期六，我和朋友莉莉一起去图书馆。我们都喜欢阅读。我们通常在那里待两个小时。首先，我们找到喜欢的书。然后我们坐在窗边阅读。图书管理员很和蔼，乐于助人。他们帮我们找到需要的书。我们在图书馆必须保持安静。我们不能在那里吃东西或奔跑。离开前，我们每人借两本书。我们可以借两星期。然后必须归还。阅读让我快乐又聪明。我想读完图书馆里的每一本书。

How long can they keep the books?

comprehension.q: What can we guess about the writer?
options: She is a person who loves reading

articles.title: Cooking with Mom
articles.text: Last Sunday, I learned to cook with my mother. We decided to make tomato and egg noodles. First, my mother showed me how to wash the tomatoes and cut them into small pieces. I was a little slow, but she was patient. Then she taught me how to break the eggs and mix them in a bowl. I was afraid of the hot oil in the pan. My mother held my hand and helped me pour the eggs in slowly. The eggs turned yellow and smelled wonderful. Next, we cooked the tomatoes with a little salt and sugar. After that, we boiled the noodles in a big pot of water. When everything was ready, we put the noodles in bowls and added the tomato and egg on top. My father and little brother tasted the noodles. They said the noodles were delicious. I felt very proud. Cooking is not easy, but it is fun. I want to learn to cook more dishes. Next time, I want to try making dumplings.
articles.textCn: 上周日，我和妈妈学做饭。我们决定做番茄鸡蛋面。首先，妈妈教我如何洗番茄并切成小块。我有点慢，但她很耐心。然后她教我如何打鸡蛋并在碗里搅拌。我害怕锅里热油。妈妈握着我的手，帮我慢慢把鸡蛋倒进去。鸡蛋变黄了，闻起来很香。接着，我们用一点盐和糖炒番茄。之后，我们在一大锅水里煮面条。一切准备好后，我们把面条放进碗里，把番茄鸡蛋加在上面。爸爸和小弟弟尝了面条。他们说面条很好吃。我感到很自豪。做饭不容易，但是很有趣。我想学做更多的菜。下次，我想试着包饺子。

articles.title: A Travel Diary
articles.text: August 15th. Today I arrived in Beijing with my parents. We came by train. The trip took five hours. We are staying in a hotel near the city center. The room is small but clean. After lunch, we went to Tian'anmen Square. It is very big and beautiful. There were many people from all over the world. We took a lot of photos. Then we walked to the Palace Museum. The old buildings are red and gold. They look wonderful. I learned that emperors lived there long ago. My father told me many interesting stories about the kings. In the evening, we had Peking duck for dinner. It was the best meal of my life. The skin was crispy and the meat was tender. Tomorrow, we will visit the Great Wall. I am very excited. My legs are tired from walking, but my heart is full of joy. Travel opens my eyes. I want to see more of the world.
articles.textCn: 8月15日。今天我和父母到了北京。我们坐火车来的。旅程花了五个小时。我们住在市中心附近的一家酒店。房间小但干净。午饭后，我们去了天安门广场。它又大又漂亮。有来自世界各地的许多人。我们拍了很多照片。然后我们走到故宫。那些古老的建筑是红色和金色的。它们看起来很壮观。我了解到很久以前皇帝住在那里。爸爸给我讲了许多关于国王的有趣故事。晚上，我们晚餐吃了北京烤鸭。那是我一生中最好的一顿饭。皮很脆，肉很嫩。明天，我们要去参观长城。我非常兴奋。我的腿走累了，但心里充满喜悦。旅行开阔了我的眼界。我想看看更多的世界。

He is curious and loves learning

articles.title: The Weather Today
articles.text: The weather changes every day. This morning, the sun was shining and the sky was blue. I wore a T-shirt and shorts to school. At noon, the wind began to blow. Dark clouds came from the west. The sky turned gray. Soon, it started to rain. The rain was heavy. We could not go out to play at recess. Some students were sad. They wanted to run in the playground. But I like rainy days. The air smells fresh after the rain. Plants look green and happy. In the afternoon, the rain stopped. A rainbow appeared in the sky. It had seven colors. articles.title: City Life vs Country Life
articles.text: Many people move from the country to the city every year. They want to find better jobs, better schools, and a more exciting life. But is city life really better than country life? Each has its own good and bad points. Cities are full of chances. There are more jobs and the pay is usually higher. There are many shops, restaurants, hospitals and schools. People can easily buy what they need. The city also has more fun places, like cinemas, parks and museums. However, city life is busy and noisy. The air is often dirty. Traffic is heavy, and people spend a lot of time on the road. Houses are very expensive, and the cost of living is high. Many people feel stressed and lonely in the city. In the country, life is slower and quieter. The air is fresh, the food is healthy, and people know their neighbors. Children can play safely outside. The cost of living is lower. But country life also has problems. There are fewer jobs, fewer schools, and fewer hospitals. It is harder to buy special things, and transport is not very convenient. In short, there is no perfect place. The best choice depends on what a person needs. Some people love the busy city, while others prefer the quiet country. Both ways of life can be happy if we choose what is right for us.
articles.textCn: 每年都有许多人从乡下搬到城市。他们想找更好的工作、更好的学校和更精彩的生活。但是城市生活真的比乡村生活更好吗？两者各有优缺点。城市充满机会。工作更多，工资通常更高。这里有很多商店、餐馆、医院和学校。人们很容易买到所需物品。城市也有更多有趣的地方，如电影院、公园和博物馆。然而，城市生活繁忙又嘈杂。空气经常很脏。交通拥挤，人们花很多时间在路上。房子很贵，生活成本很高。许多人在城市里感到有压力和孤独。在乡村，生活更慢更安静。空气清新，食物健康，人们认识自己的邻居。孩子们可以在外面安全地玩耍。生活成本更低。但乡村生活也有问题。工作、学校和医院更少。买到特殊物品更难，交通也不太方便。简而言之，没有完美的地方。最好的选择取决于一个人的需求。有些人喜欢繁忙的城市，而另一些人更喜欢安静的乡村。两种生活方式都可以幸福，只要我们选择适合自己的。

articles.title: A Memorable Train Journey
articles.text: Last summer, I took a long train journey across the country. I went with my grandfather to visit his old hometown. We left early in the morning. The train was big and comfortable. Our seats were next to the window. As the train moved, I watched the world outside. The view changed all the time. We passed green fields, small villages, deep forests and wide rivers. Sometimes we went through dark tunnels under big mountains. The train was not very full, so it was quiet. My grandfather told me many stories about his youth. He told me how he left his village when he was eighteen, with only a small bag and little money. He worked hard in the city for many years. Now he wanted to see his old home one more time. After twelve hours, we arrived. The old house was still there, but the village had changed a lot. We met an old neighbor who remembered my grandfather. They talked for a long time and laughed together. We stayed for two days. We ate simple country food and walked on the old roads. On the way back, my grandfather was very quiet. I could see he was happy, but also a little sad. This journey taught me that home is more than a place. It is the people and the memories we love. I will never forget this trip.

articles.title: Protecting Our Environment
articles.text: Our planet is facing many environmental problems. The air is getting dirtier. The rivers and seas are full of plastic waste. Forests are being cut down. Many animals are losing their homes. Some are dying out forever. If we do not act now, our children will live in a broken world. The good news is that everyone can help. Even small actions make a difference. First, we can reduce what we use. We can bring our own bags when we go shopping. We can use a water bottle many times instead of buying new plastic ones. Second, we can reuse things. Old clothes can become cleaning cloths. Glass jars can hold small objects. Third, we can recycle. Paper, glass, metal and plastic can all be turned into new things. Many cities have recycling bins on the streets. We only need to sort our waste carefully. Fourth, we can save energy. Turn off the lights when we leave a room. Walk or ride a bike instead of driving. Plant trees in our neighborhoods. Trees clean the air and give homes to birds. Schools and governments also have a big role to play. Schools can teach children to love nature. Governments can make laws to stop factories from polluting. Some countries have already banned plastic bags. Others are investing in clean energy like wind and solar power. However, laws are not enough. Real change begins in our daily choices. Some people think one person cannot make a difference. But when millions of people make small changes, the result is huge. The earth does not belong to us. We borrow it from our children. It is our duty to return it in good condition. Protecting the environment is not just a job for scientists or leaders. It is a job for every one of us, every single day.
articles.textCn: 我们的星球正面临许多环境问题。空气越来越脏。河流和海洋满是塑料垃圾。森林被砍伐。许多动物正在失去家园。有些正在永远灭绝。如果我们现在不行动，我们的孩子将生活在一个破碎的世界里。好消息是每个人都能帮忙。即使小小的行动也有意义。首先，我们可以减少使用。购物时可以自带袋子。我们可以多次使用水瓶，而不是买新的塑料瓶。其次，我们可以重复使用物品。旧衣服可以变成抹布。玻璃罐可以装小物件。第三，我们可以回收。纸张、玻璃、金属和塑料都可以变成新东西。许多城市街上有回收桶。我们只需要仔细分类垃圾。第四，我们可以节约能源。离开房间时关灯。走路或骑车代替开车。在社区种树。树木净化空气，给鸟类提供家园。学校和政府也有重要作用。学校可以教孩子热爱自然。政府可以制定法律阻止工厂污染。一些国家已经禁止塑料袋。另一些正在投资风能和太阳能等清洁能源。然而，法律还不够。真正的改变始于我们的日常选择。有些人认为一个人不能改变什么。但当数百万人做出小小的改变时，结果是巨大的。地球不属于我们。我们是从孩子那里借来的。我们有责任以良好的状态归还它。保护环境不仅是科学家或领导人的工作。这是我们每个人每天的工作。

articles.title: Following My Dream
articles.text: When I was eight years old, I wanted to be a doctor. When I was twelve, I wanted to be a writer. Now I am seventeen, and I want to be a teacher. My dream has changed many times. But one thing has never changed. I have always wanted to do something meaningful with my life. Many people told me that dreams are just dreams. They said I should be realistic. They told me to choose a safe job that pays well. For a while, I listened to them. I tried to study subjects I did not like. I felt unhappy and tired. My grades were not good. I could not sleep well at night. Then I met a teacher who changed my thinking. Her name is Ms. Chen. She told me her own story. When she was young, her family wanted her to study business. But she loved literature. She worked hard and finally became a literature teacher. She told me, follow your heart, but work harder than anyone else. Dreams without effort are only wishes. Dreams with effort become goals. After that talk, I made a decision. I would follow my dream to become a teacher. I started to study education and psychology. I read many books. I also began to help younger students with their homework. The work was hard, but I felt happy inside. I was no longer tired and lost. I knew what I was working for. The road ahead is long. There will be many difficulties. Some people will still tell me to be realistic. But I have learned an important lesson. A life without a dream is like a ship without a compass. You may move, but you do not know where you are going. I know where I am going now. And I will not stop until I get there.
articles.textCn: 当我八岁时，我想当医生。当我十二岁时，我想当作家。现在我十七岁，我想当老师。我的梦想改变了很多次。但有一件事从未改变。我一直想用我的生命做有意义的事。许多人告诉我梦想只是梦想。他们说我应该现实。他们让我选择一份安全、收入好的工作。有一段时间，我听了他们的话。我试图学习我不喜欢的科目。我感到不开心和疲惫。我的成绩不好。我晚上睡不好。后来我遇到了一位改变我想法的老师。她叫陈老师。她告诉了我她自己的故事。她年轻时，家人想让她学商科。但她热爱文学。她努力学习，最终成为了一名文学老师。她告诉我，跟随你的心，但比任何人都更努力。没有努力梦想只是愿望。有努力梦想才成为目标。那次谈话后，我做出了决定。我要追随成为老师的梦想。我开始学习教育学和心理学。我读了很多书。我也开始帮年纪小的学生做作业。工作很辛苦，但我内心感到快乐。我不再疲惫和迷茫。我知道我在为什么努力。前方的路还很长。会有很多困难。有些人仍会告诉我现实一点。但我学到了重要的一课。没有梦想的生活就像没有指南针的船。你可能移动，但不知道去哪里。我现在知道我要去哪里。我不会停下，直到到达。

articles.title: The Power of Teamwork
articles.text: Last month, our school held a basketball competition. Each class had to send a team. I was chosen as the captain of our class team. At first, I was worried. Our team was not the strongest. Some students were short. Some were not good at sports. Two of our best players were sick. We had only one week to prepare. I decided that we could not win by strength alone. We had to win by working together. So I made a plan. Every day after school, we practiced for two hours. But we did not just practice shooting. We practiced passing, defending, and trusting each other. I told my teammates that no one could win alone. If one of us fell, the others would cover for him. If one was open, the one with the ball would pass. The first practice was messy. People argued. Some did not want to pass. One boy even wanted to quit. I sat down with the team and talked for a long time. I told them that we were not just a team for one week. We were a family. The next day, something changed. People began to listen to each other. They passed the ball more. They helped each other on defense. Slowly, our team began to play like one person, not five separate players. On the day of the competition, we were nervous. The other teams were taller and faster. But we played our game. We passed the ball quickly. We defended together. We never gave up, even when we were behind. In the final game, we were losing by five points. In the last two minutes, we scored seven points and won. Everyone was cheering. We were not the strongest team, but we were the closest team. That day, I learned something that I will never forget. Talent is important, but teamwork is more powerful. One person can do good things. But a team that trusts each other can do great things. This lesson does not only work in sports. It works in study, in work, and in life. When we help each other, we all go further.
articles.textCn: 上个月，我们学校举办了一场篮球比赛。每个班都要派一支队伍。我被选为我们班的队长。起初，我很担心。我们的队伍不是最强的。一些学生矮。一些不擅长运动。我们最好的两个球员病了。我们只有一周时间准备。我决定我们不能只靠力量取胜。我们必须靠合作取胜。所以我制定了计划。每天放学后，我们练习两个小时。但我们不只练习投篮。我们练习传球、防守和互相信任。我告诉队友，没有人能独自取胜。如果一个人倒下，其他人会补上。如果一个人有空位，持球的人会传球。第一次练习很乱。人们争吵。一些不愿传球。一个男孩甚至想退出。我和队伍坐下来谈了很久。我告诉他们，我们不仅仅是一周的队伍。我们是一家人。第二天，情况改变了。人们开始互相倾听。他们更多传球。在防守上互相帮助。慢慢地，我们的队伍开始像一个人在打球，而不是五个独立的球员。比赛那天，我们很紧张。其他队伍更高更快。但我们打我们的比赛。我们快速传球。一起防守。即使落后也从不放弃。在决赛中，我们落后五分。在最后两分钟，我们得了七分，赢了。每个人都在欢呼。我们不是最强的队伍，但我们是最团结的队伍。那天，我学到了永生难忘的东西。天赋重要，但团队合作更强大。一个人能做好事。但互相信任的团队能做伟大的事。这个教训不仅在体育中有效。在学习、工作和生活中都有效。当我们互相帮助时，我们都能走得更远。

articles.title: Cultural Exchange
articles.text: Last year, my school started a cultural exchange program. Every spring, a group of students from France comes to our city. They stay with Chinese families for two weeks. At the same time, some of our students go to France. I was lucky to be chosen. A French boy named Lucas came to stay with my family. At first, we could not understand each other well. His English was not perfect, and my French was almost zero. We used our phones to translate. We pointed at things and smiled a lot. Slowly, we found ways to talk. I taught him how to use chopsticks. He taught me how to make a simple French dish. I took him to see the Great Wall and the Palace Museum. He was amazed by the long history of China. He took photos of everything. He said Chinese food was different from what he imagined, but he loved it. In return, he told me stories about Paris. He showed me pictures of the Eiffel Tower and French bread. He taught me a few French words. I learned that culture is not just about big things like buildings and history. Culture is also about small things. How we greet each other. What we eat for breakfast. How we show respect to older people. These small things are different in every country. But the differences are not bad. They are interesting. They make the world rich and colorful. When Lucas left, we both cried a little. We promised to keep in touch. We still write to each other every month. This experience changed how I see the world. Before, other countries seemed far and strange. Now, they feel closer. I learned that people everywhere have the same feelings. We all want friends. We all want to understand and be understood. If more young people could have such exchanges, the world would be more peaceful. Differences are not walls. They are doors. We only need the courage to open them.
articles.textCn: 去年，我们学校启动了一个文化交流项目。每年春天，一群来自法国的学生来到我们城市。他们在中国家庭住两周。同时，我们的一些学生去法国。我很幸运被选中。一个叫卢卡斯的法国男孩来我家住。起初，我们不太能理解彼此。他的英语不完美，我的法语几乎为零。我们用手机翻译。我们指东西，微笑很多。慢慢地，我们找到了交流的方式。我教他用筷子。他教我做一道简单的法国菜。我带他去看了长城和故宫。他对中国悠久的历史感到惊叹。他什么都拍照。他说中国食物和他想象的不同，但他很喜欢。作为回报，他给我讲了巴黎的故事。给我看了埃菲尔铁塔和法国面包的照片。他教了我几个法语单词。我了解到，文化不仅仅是建筑和历史这样的大事。文化也是小事。我们如何打招呼。早餐吃什么。如何对长辈表示尊重。这些小事在每个国家都不同。但不同不是坏事。它们很有趣。它们让世界丰富多彩。卢卡斯离开时，我们都哭了。我们答应保持联系。我们仍然每个月通信。这次经历改变了我看世界的方式。以前，其他国家显得遥远陌生。现在，它们感觉更近了。我了解到，各地的人都有相同的感受。我们都想要朋友。我们都想理解和被理解。如果更多年轻人能有这样的交流，世界会更和平。差异不是墙。它们是门。我们只需要勇气去打开它们。

articles.title: The Joy of Reading
articles.text: I was not always a reader. When I was young, I did not like books. I thought they were boring and slow. I preferred to watch television or play games. My friends felt the same way. Then one rainy day, when I was ten, the power went out. There was no television, no games, no internet. I was so bored that I picked up a book from the shelf. It was a story about a boy who found a magic tree. The tree could take him to different worlds. I read the first page, then the second, then the third. Before I knew it, I had read ten chapters. When the power came back, I did not even notice. I kept reading until I finished the whole book. That was the day my life changed. From then on, I read every day. I read in the morning before school. I read during lunch. I read before bed. I read on the bus. Books became my best friends. Through books, I traveled to places I had never been. I visited ancient Egypt, future cities, and distant stars. I met kings and queens, heroes and cowards, wise teachers and foolish kings. Books taught me about the world and about myself. They taught me that life is more than what I see around me. They taught me that every person has a story worth hearing. They taught me to think, to ask questions, and to dream. Reading also improved my language. My vocabulary grew. My writing became clearer. I could express my thoughts better. My teachers noticed the change. Reading is not always easy. Some books are hard. Some ideas take time to understand. But that is part of the joy. When you finally understand a difficult idea, you feel like you have climbed a mountain. The view from the top is worth the climb. If you do not read yet, I want to tell you this. Start small. Find a book about something you love. Give it twenty pages before you decide. You may be surprised. A whole new world may open up to you, just as it did for me on that rainy day.
articles.textCn: 我以前并不总是爱读书的人。小时候，我不喜欢书。我觉得它们无聊又慢。我更喜欢看电视或玩游戏。我的朋友们也一样。后来一个十岁的雨天，停电了。没有电视、没有游戏、没有网络。我太无聊了，从书架上拿起一本书。那是一个男孩发现一棵神奇树的故事。那棵树能带他到不同的世界。我读了第一页，然后第二页，第三页。不知不觉中，我读了十章。当电来的时候，我都没注意到。我一直读到读完整本书。那天我的生活改变了。从那以后，我每天读书。早上上学前读。午饭时读。睡前读。在公交车上读。书成了我最好的朋友。通过书，我到了从未去过的地方。我访问了古埃及、未来城市和遥远的星球。我遇见了国王和王后、英雄和懦夫、睿智的老师和愚蠢的国王。书教会我了解世界和自己。它们教会我，生活不仅仅是我周围看到的。它们教会我每个人都有值得听的故事。它们教会我思考、提问和梦想。阅读也改善了我的语言。我的词汇量增长了。写作更清晰了。我能更好地表达想法。老师们注意到了变化。阅读并不总是容易的。有些书很难。有些想法需要时间理解。但那是乐趣的一部分。当你终于理解了一个困难的想法，你感觉像爬上了一座山。山顶的风景值得攀登。如果你还不读书，我想告诉你。从小开始。找一本关于你喜欢的东西的书。决定前给它二十页。你可能会惊讶。一个全新的世界可能向你打开，就像那个雨天对我一样。

articles.title: The Importance of Friends
articles.text: Friends are important in our lives. They share our happiness. They share our sadness. They help us when we are in trouble. Good friends are honest. They tell us the truth. They do not talk behind our backs. Good friends are loyal. They stay with us in good times and bad times. Good friends are supportive. They encourage us when we doubt ourselves. To have good friends, we must be a good friend first. We should listen. We should care. We should be there when they need us. Friendship is a treasure. We should cherish it. With good friends, life is richer and more meaningful.

articles.title: How to Be a Good Student
articles.text: Being a good student is not just about getting good grades. It is about learning well. Here are some tips. First, be organized. Keep a planner. Write down your homework. Don't forget. articles.text: Health is the most important thing in life. Without it, nothing else matters. Here are some ways to stay healthy. First, eat well. Eat lots of fruit and vegetables. Eat less junk food. articles.title: The Art of Conversation
articles.text: Conversation is an art that many of us have forgotten. In the age of texts and emails, we have lost the ability to talk deeply. But good conversation is one of life's great pleasures. It connects us. It enriches us. It makes us feel alive. To have good conversations, we need to master a few skills. First, listen. Really listen. Don't just wait for your turn to speak. Pay attention to what the other person is saying. Try to understand their perspective. Show that you are listening with your body language. Nod. Make eye contact. Second, ask questions. Good questions show interest. They keep the conversation going. Ask open-ended questions that cannot be answered with yes or no. Ask about their opinions, their experiences, their feelings. Third, share. Conversation is a two-way street. Share your own stories. But don't dominate. Balance listening and sharing. Fourth, be present. Don't look at your phone. Don't think about other things. Be there, fully. Fifth, be authentic. Don't pretend to be someone you are not. People can tell. Be yourself. Sixth, be respectful. Even if you disagree, respect the other person. Don't attack them. Don't insult them. Seventh, be curious. Everyone has a story. Everyone has something to teach you. Approach every conversation with curiosity. Eighth, practice. The more you talk, the better you get. Talk to different people. Try different topics. With time, you will become a master of conversation. And your relationships will deepen. Your life will be richer.

articles.title: The Story of the Internet
articles.text: The Internet has changed the world. It has changed how we communicate, learn, work, and play. But how did it begin? The Internet started in the 1960s as a military project. The U.S. military wanted a network that could survive a nuclear attack. They created ARPANET. It connected computers at universities and research labs. In 1969, the first message was sent. It was supposed to be 'LOGIN,' but the system crashed after two letters. The first message was 'LO.' In the 1970s, scientists developed TCP/IP, a way for different networks to communicate. This was the birth of the Internet. But it was hard to use. There were no pictures, no colors, just text. In 1989, Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web. It used hyperlinks to connect documents. This made the Internet accessible to everyone. In 1993, the Web was released to the public for free. The Internet exploded. Amazon, eBay, Google, Facebook, YouTube—all were founded in the following years. Each changed a part of our lives. The Internet changed how we shop, learn, work, communicate, and play. It changed politics and business. It changed our psychology. We are always connected. We check our phones constantly. We compare our lives to others. This has affected our mental health. The Internet is still evolving. Mobile Internet made it always with us. Social media made it participatory. AI is making it intelligent. The story of the Internet is still being written. It is a tool for empowerment and for control. For connection and for isolation. For truth and for lies. The future depends on how we use it. The choice is ours.

articles.text: Public speaking is one of the most feared things in the world. Many people fear it more than death. Yet it is also one of the most valuable skills. Practice until you know your speech by heart. Sixth, use your body language. Stand tall. Make eye contact. Use your hands. Move around the stage. Your body speaks as loudly as your words. articles.title: The Art of Time Management
articles.text: Time is our most valuable resource. We all have 24 hours a day. Yet some people achieve much more than others. The difference is time management. Good time management is not about being busy. It is about being effective. The first step is to know your goals. What do you want to achieve? Long-term, medium-term, short-term. Write them down. Goals give direction. Without them, you waste time on things that don't matter. The second step is to prioritize. The Eisenhower Matrix is a useful tool. It divides tasks into four categories. Urgent and important—do now. Important but not urgent—schedule. Urgent but not important—delegate. Neither urgent nor important—eliminate. Many people spend too much time on urgent but unimportant tasks. The third step is to plan. Make a daily plan. Make a weekly plan. Make a monthly plan. A plan helps you focus. It reduces decision fatigue. The fourth step is to avoid distractions. Turn off notifications. Close unnecessary tabs. Put your phone in another room. Distractions are the enemy of focus. The fifth step is to use techniques. The Pomodoro Technique works in 25-minute focus blocks with 5-minute breaks. Time blocking assigns specific tasks to specific times. The two-minute rule says if a task takes less than two minutes, do it now. The sixth step is to manage energy, not just time. We have peak energy times. For most people, it's the morning. Do your hardest tasks then. Do easier tasks in the afternoon. The seventh step is to say no. Every yes is a no to something else. Learn to decline requests that don't align with your goals. The eighth step is to delegate. You don't have to do everything. Delegate tasks that others can do. This frees you to do what only you can do. The ninth step is to take breaks. The brain cannot focus for hours. Breaks restore focus. They prevent burnout. The tenth step is to review. At the end of each day, review what you did. At the end of each week, review your progress. Adjust as needed. Good time management is a skill. It takes practice. But it pays off. You achieve more. You stress less. You have time for what matters. Time is limited. Use it well.

articles.title: The Story of Cities
articles.text: Cities are one of humanity's greatest inventions. They are where ideas are born. Where cultures mix. Where economies grow. The first cities appeared about 6,000 years ago. They were in Mesopotamia, Egypt, India, and China. Uruk, in Mesopotamia, was one of the first. It had 50,000 people. Cities grew because of agriculture. Farming produced surplus food. Not everyone had to farm. Some could specialize. They became artisans, merchants, priests, soldiers. Cities became centers of trade. They became centers of power. They became centers of learning. Ancient Athens was a city of ideas. Philosophy, democracy, theater—all flourished. Ancient Rome was a city of engineering. Aqueducts, roads, buildings—the Romans built to last. In the Middle Ages, cities were smaller. But they were still important. Constantinople, Baghdad, Chang'an—these were great cities. They were centers of trade and learning. The Renaissance brought new ideas to cities. Florence, Venice, Genoa—they financed explorers and artists. The Industrial Revolution changed cities. Factories were built in cities. People moved from farms to cities. Cities grew rapidly. London, New York, Tokyo—they exploded in size. This growth brought problems. Overcrowding. Pollution. Disease. Crime. Reformers fought back. They built parks. They improved sanitation. They built subways. In the 20th century, cities kept growing. Skyscrapers made them taller. Cars made them spread out. Suburbs grew. Some cities declined. Detroit, St. Louis, Glasgow—they lost industries and people. Other cities thrived. Silicon Valley, Bangalore, Shenzhen—they became tech hubs. Today, more than half the world's population lives in cities. By 2050, it will be two-thirds. Cities face challenges. Housing is expensive. Traffic is bad. Pollution is high. Inequality is stark. Climate change threatens coastal cities. But cities also offer solutions. They are more efficient. Per person, cities use less energy. They produce more ideas. They offer more opportunities. Cities are where the future will be decided. Smart cities use technology to improve life. Sensors monitor traffic. Apps guide drivers to parking. Drones deliver packages. Autonomous buses move people. Cities are also becoming greener. Parks are being added. Rivers are being restored. Bike lanes are being built. Renewable energy is being used. The city of the future will be different. It will be denser. It will be smarter. It will be greener. It will be more inclusive. The story of cities is the story of civilization. From Uruk to Tokyo, cities have shaped us. And we have shaped them. The next chapter is being written now.

articles.title: The Psychology of Happiness
articles.text: What makes us happy? This question has been asked for thousands of years. Philosophers, religious leaders, and now scientists have sought answers. The science of happiness is called positive psychology. It studies what makes life worth living. Researchers have found some surprising things. First, money matters less than we think. Money does buy happiness, but only up to a point. Once basic needs are met, more money does not bring more happiness. Studies show that lottery winners are not much happier than others. Second, circumstances matter less than we think. We think we would be happier if we were richer, taller, or more attractive. But studies show these have small effects. Third, what matters most is what we do and how we think. The biggest factor in happiness is relationships. People with strong relationships are happier. This is the longest-running study on happiness. Harvard studied men for 80 years. The finding was clear. Good relationships keep us happier and healthier. Fourth, gratitude increases happiness. People who regularly count their blessings are happier. They are more optimistic. They are more satisfied with life. Fifth, kindness increases happiness. Helping others makes us happy. Even small acts of kindness boost our mood. Sixth, exercise increases happiness. Regular exercise is as effective as medication for mild depression. It releases endorphins. It improves our mood. Seventh, sleep increases happiness. Lack of sleep makes us irritable and sad. Good sleep improves our emotional state. Eighth, meaning increases happiness. People who feel their lives have purpose are happier. This can come from work, family, religion, or a cause. Ninth, flow increases happiness. Flow is being completely absorbed in an activity. We lose track of time. This can happen in work, hobbies, or sports. Tenth, mindfulness increases happiness. Being present reduces anxiety. It helps us enjoy the moment. Happiness is not constant. We all feel sad sometimes. That is normal. But we can build habits that increase our baseline happiness. We can nurture relationships. We can practice gratitude. We can be kind. We can exercise. We can seek meaning. We can be mindful. Happiness is not a destination. It is a way of traveling. It is not something that happens to us. It is something we create. The science of happiness teaches us that we have more control than we think. We can choose habits that make us happier. And in doing so, we can live richer, more fulfilling lives.

articles.title: The Story of Transportation
articles.text: Transportation has shaped human history. It determines where we live, where we work, and how we connect. The story of transportation is the story of civilization. Early humans walked. They carried what they could. Then they domesticated animals. Horses, donkeys, oxen, and camels carried loads. They pulled carts. They allowed people to travel farther and faster. The wheel was invented around 3500 BC. It revolutionized transport. Carts and chariots became common. Roads were built. The Romans built the best roads. Their network stretched across Europe. Roads enabled trade, armies, and ideas to move. Ships also transformed transportation. The first boats were canoes. They were used on rivers. Then came sails. Sails allowed ships to cross oceans. The Phoenicians, Greeks, and Vikings were skilled sailors. They traded across the Mediterranean, the Atlantic, and beyond. In the 15th century, Europeans explored the world. Portuguese ships reached India. Spanish ships crossed the Atlantic. Columbus reached the Americas. Magellan's crew sailed around the world. These voyages changed history. They connected continents. They spread diseases. They enabled colonization. The Industrial Revolution transformed transportation again. Steam engines powered ships and trains. Trains could carry heavy loads over long distances. They were faster than horses. They changed where people lived. Cities grew along rail lines. The transcontinental railroad connected American coasts. It took only days instead of months. In the late 19th century, the automobile was invented. At first, it was a toy for the rich. Henry Ford made it affordable. The Model T changed America. People could live farther from work. Suburbs grew. Highways were built. The car became a symbol of freedom. In 1903, the Wright brothers flew. Aviation was born. Planes were first used in war. Then they carried passengers. Jet engines made flights fast. By the 21st century, millions flew every day. Aviation connected the world. A trip that took months now took hours. In the 21st century, transportation is changing again. Electric cars are replacing gasoline cars. They are cleaner and quieter. Self-driving cars are being developed. They could reduce accidents. They could give freedom to people who cannot drive. Ride-sharing services changed how we use cars. Many people no longer own cars. High-speed trains are connecting cities. In Japan, the Shinkansen carries millions. In Europe, trains cross borders in hours. In China, the high-speed rail network is the world's largest. Space travel is also advancing. Rockets that can be reused are lowering costs. Private companies are building spacecraft. Space tourism is becoming real. The future of transportation is being written. It will be cleaner. It will be smarter. It will be faster. But challenges remain. Traffic jams waste time. Pollution harms health. Accidents kill millions. Transportation also divides. Rich areas have good transport. Poor areas do not. Transportation will continue to shape our world. It will determine how we live, work, and connect. Its story is our story.

articles.title: The Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
articles.text: Artificial intelligence, or AI, has developed rapidly in the past twenty years. Today it can drive cars, write articles, translate languages, and even create art. Many people welcome these changes because they make our lives easier and more productive. However, the rise of AI also raises serious ethical questions that we cannot ignore. The first question is about jobs. As machines become smarter, they can do more and more work that used to belong to humans. Factory workers, drivers, and even some doctors and lawyers may lose their jobs to AI. If many people cannot find work, society will face deep problems. We need to think about how to help these people, perhaps by giving them new skills or by sharing the wealth that AI creates. The second question is about responsibility. When an AI system makes a mistake, who is to blame? If a self-driving car crashes into someone, is the company that built the car responsible? Or is it the person who owns the car? Or the AI itself? Our laws are not yet ready to answer these questions clearly. The third question is about fairness. AI systems learn from large amounts of data. If that data is biased, the AI will also be biased. For example, some AI tools have been unfair to women or to people from certain races, because the data they learned from was unfair. This can lead to real harm in hiring, lending, and justice. The fourth question is about privacy. AI can collect and study huge amounts of personal information. Without strong rules, our private lives may become a product sold to the highest bidder. Despite these concerns, we should not stop developing AI. The technology can also solve many great problems, such as curing diseases and protecting the environment. The key is to build AI carefully, with clear rules and human oversight. We must ensure that AI serves human beings, not the other way around. If we act wisely, AI can be one of the best tools we have ever created.

articles.title: Climate Change: A Global Crisis
articles.titleCn: 气候变化：一场全球危机
articles.text: Climate change is one of the greatest challenges of our time. For more than a hundred years, humans have burned coal, oil, and gas to power factories, cars, and homes. This has released huge amounts of gases into the air. These gases trap the heat of the sun and slowly warm the earth. The results are now clear to everyone. The world is getting warmer. Ice at the North and South Poles is melting. Sea levels are rising. Some lands near the sea may disappear under water in the coming decades. Many places suffer from stronger storms, longer droughts, and more sudden floods. Animals and plants that cannot adapt quickly are dying out. Poor people, who have done the least to cause this problem, often suffer the most. Scientists have warned us for many years. They say we must act fast. The good news is that many countries are now working together. They have signed agreements to reduce the gases they release. They are also building more wind and solar power to replace coal and oil. Electric cars are becoming common, and forests are being planted again. However, this is not enough. Big changes are still slow. Some rich countries have not done their share. Some companies still put profit before the planet. Each of us can also help. We can use less energy at home. We can walk, bike, or take buses instead of driving. We can eat less meat, because meat production uses a lot of land and water. We can buy fewer things and reuse what we have. We can also vote for leaders who care about the earth. Climate change is not a problem for the future. It is here, right now. If we do not act together, our children and grandchildren will pay a terrible price. The earth is the only home we have. We must protect it before it is too late.

articles.title: The Evolution of Social Media
articles.text: Social media has changed the way we talk, think, and live. Twenty years ago, the word social media did not even exist. People kept in touch by phone, letter, or face to face. Today, billions of people use platforms every day to share photos, news, and feelings. The story of social media shows how fast the world can change. The first social sites appeared in the early 2000s. They were simple. People used them mostly to chat with old friends or to meet new ones. Then came the age of sharing. New sites let users post photos and short messages. Suddenly, anyone could speak to the whole world for free. This was a kind of freedom never seen before. Activists used it to organize protests. Small businesses reached customers across oceans. Quiet people found their voice. But every tool has two sides. The same speed that brought people together also spread false news. The same freedom that gave everyone a voice also brought hate and lies. People began to spend hours every day looking at screens. They compared their real lives to the perfect pictures others posted. Many began to feel sad, anxious, or less worthy. Young people were hit the hardest. Their brains were still growing, and they cared deeply about what others thought of them. Today, social media is trying to fix some of these problems. Some sites now warn users about false news or limit time for children. Governments are writing new rules to protect privacy and data. Schools are teaching children how to think critically about what they see online. The future of social media is not yet written. It may become more honest, or it may become more dangerous. What is certain is that it will not go away. We must learn to use it with wisdom, not let it use us. Like fire, social media can warm a house or burn it down. The choice is ours. We should teach our children to hold this tool carefully, to question what they read, and to remember that real life happens off the screen as well as on it.
articles.textCn: 社交媒体改变了我们说话、思考和生活的方式。二十年前，社交媒体这个词甚至还不存在。人们通过电话、信件或面对面保持联系。今天，数十亿人每天使用平台分享照片、新闻和感受。社交媒体的故事展示了世界变化有多快。第一批社交网站出现在2000年代初。它们很简单。人们主要用它们和老朋友聊天或认识新朋友。然后是分享时代。新网站让用户发布照片和短消息。突然之间，任何人都能免费向全世界讲话。这是一种前所未有的自由。活动家用它组织抗议。小企业跨越海洋接触客户。安静的人找到了自己的声音。但每种工具都有两面。把人们聚集在一起的同样速度也传播了虚假新闻。赋予每个人声音的同样自由也带来了仇恨和谎言。人们开始每天花数小时看屏幕。他们把自己的真实生活与别人发布的完美照片比较。许多人开始感到悲伤、焦虑或觉得自己不如人。年轻人受影响最深。他们的大脑还在发育，他们深切关心别人对自己的看法。今天，社交媒体正试图解决其中一些问题。一些网站现在警告用户虚假新闻，或限制儿童使用时间。政府正在制定新规则保护隐私和数据。学校正在教孩子们如何批判性地思考他们在网上看到的内容。社交媒体的未来尚未书写。它可能变得更诚实，也可能变得更危险。可以肯定的是，它不会消失。我们必须学会明智地使用它，而不是让它使用我们。像火一样，社交媒体可以温暖房屋也可以烧毁它。选择权在我们手中。我们应该教我们的孩子小心地握住这个工具，质疑他们所读到的内容，并记住真实生活既发生在屏幕外，也发生在屏幕上。

articles.title: Work-Life Balance in Modern Society
articles.titleCn: 现代社会的工作与生活平衡
articles.text: In modern society, many people find it hard to balance their work and their personal life. They wake up early, work all day, come home tired, and have little time for family, friends, or themselves. This problem has become worse in recent years. Some people say the cause is technology. Fifty years ago, when workers left the office, their work was done. Today, with phones and laptops, work follows us everywhere. The boss can send a message at any time of day or night. Many workers feel they must answer quickly, or they may lose their jobs. The line between work and rest has almost disappeared. Others say the cause is the economy. Prices of houses, food, and education have risen faster than wages. Many young people work long hours just to pay for a small apartment. Some hold two or three jobs at the same time. They have no choice, they say, because life is too expensive. Still others blame culture. In some countries, people who leave work early are seen as lazy. Workers fear that if they rest, others will pass them by. So they work hard, even when they are sick or tired. The cost of this imbalance is serious. Many workers become sick with stress, sleep problems, or sadness. Marriages suffer. Children grow up rarely seeing their parents. Old people grow lonely because their busy children cannot visit. Companies also pay a price. Tired workers make more mistakes. They invent less. They leave their jobs more often. Smart companies have noticed this. Some now offer flexible hours, more days off, or the chance to work from home. Studies show that workers who rest well do better work. They are also happier and stay longer with the same company. Each person also has a part to play. We can learn to say no to extra work that is not truly needed. We can put our phones away during meals and family time. We can take short breaks during the day to walk or breathe. Health and love are more important than any job. A balanced life is not only better for the worker. It is better for everyone. We must remember that we work in order to live, not live in order to work.
articles.textCn: 在现代社会，许多人发现很难平衡工作和个人生活。他们早早起床，工作一整天，疲惫地回家，几乎没有时间留给家人、朋友或自己。这个问题近年来变得更严重。有人说原因是技术。五十年前，工人离开办公室，工作就结束了。今天，有了手机和笔记本电脑，工作到处跟着我们。老板可以在白天或晚上的任何时间发消息。许多工人觉得必须快速回复，否则可能失去工作。工作和休息之间的界限几乎消失了。另一些人说原因是经济。房子、食物和教育的价格比工资涨得快。许多年轻人长时间工作只是为了付一套小公寓的钱。一些人同时做两三份工作。他们说别无选择，因为生活太贵了。还有人归咎于文化。在一些国家，早下班的人被视为懒惰。工人害怕如果他们休息，别人会超过他们。所以他们拼命工作，即使生病或疲惫。这种失衡的代价是严重的。许多工人因压力、睡眠问题或悲伤而生病。婚姻受到影响。孩子们在成长中很少见到父母。老人变得孤独，因为他们忙碌的子女无法探望。公司也付出代价。疲惫的工人犯更多错误。他们创新更少。他们更频繁地离职。聪明的公司注意到了这一点。一些公司现在提供弹性工作时间、更多休息日或在家工作的机会。研究表明，休息好的工人工作做得更好。他们也更快乐，在同一家公司待得更久。每个人也有自己的责任。我们可以学会拒绝不必要的额外工作。我们可以在用餐和家庭时间把手机放一边。我们可以在一天中休息片刻去散步或呼吸。健康和爱比任何工作都重要。平衡的生活不仅对工人更好。它对每个人都更好。我们必须记住，我们工作是为了生活，而不是生活是为了工作。

articles.title: The Future of Remote Work
articles.text: A few years ago, most people went to an office every day to do their work. Remote work, or working from home, was rare. Some companies allowed it for one or two days a week, but most workers had never tried it. Then a great disease spread across the world, and everything changed in a few weeks. Millions of people were sent home to work. At first, many were worried. They did not know if work could be done well outside the office. They missed their coworkers and the clear line between work and home. But soon, both workers and companies found that remote work had many good points. Workers saved the time and money they used to spend on travel. They could wake up later, eat better food, and spend more time with their families. Some moved out of expensive cities to quieter, cheaper places. Companies found that work was still getting done. They could also save money on office space and hire talented people from anywhere in the world. However, remote work is not perfect. Many workers feel lonely without their coworkers. New employees find it hard to learn the culture of the company. Some people cannot separate work from rest, because the office is also their home. They work too much and grow tired. Children at home can make it hard to focus. Not every home has a quiet room or a fast internet connection. Today, many companies are choosing a middle path. They ask workers to come to the office two or three days a week and work from home the rest of the time. This is called hybrid work. It tries to keep the good parts of both worlds. The future is still not clear. Some experts believe that most work will become remote, while others think people will return to offices. The truth may lie somewhere between. What is sure is that workers now expect more freedom than before. Companies that offer no flexibility may lose their best people. In the end, the future of work will be shaped not only by technology but also by what workers and companies learn to value. The most successful will be those who can change with the times while still caring for the people who do the work.
articles.textCn: 几年前，大多数人每天去办公室工作。远程工作，或在家工作，很罕见。一些公司每周允许一两天，但大多数工人从未尝试过。然后，一种大疾病席卷世界，几周内一切都变了。数百万人被送回家工作。起初，许多人担心。他们不知道工作能否在办公室外做好。他们想念同事，也想念工作和家庭之间清晰的界限。但很快，工人和公司都发现远程工作有很多优点。工人节省了过去花在通勤上的时间和金钱。他们可以更晚起床，吃更好的食物，和家人共度更多时间。一些人搬离昂贵的城市，去更安静、更便宜的地方。公司发现工作仍然在完成。他们也能节省办公空间的钱，并从世界任何地方雇佣有才华的人。然而，远程工作并不完美。许多工人没有同事会感到孤独。新员工发现很难学习公司文化。一些人无法将工作和休息分开，因为办公室也是他们的家。他们工作太多，变得疲惫。家里的孩子可能让人难以集中注意力。不是每个家都有安静的房间或快速的网络连接。今天，许多公司选择中间道路。他们要求工人每周来办公室两三天，其余时间在家工作。这叫做混合工作。它试图保留两个世界的优点。未来仍不明朗。一些专家认为大多数工作将变得远程，而另一些人认为人们会回到办公室。真相可能在两者之间。可以肯定的是，工人现在比以前期望更多自由。不提供灵活性的公司可能失去最优秀的人。最终，工作的未来不仅由技术塑造，也由工人和公司学会重视的东西塑造。最成功的将是那些能与时俱进，同时仍然关心做工作的人的人。

articles.title: Education Reform for the 21st Century
articles.text: Most schools today still look very much like schools a hundred years ago. Children sit in rows. They listen to a teacher at the front. They memorize facts. They take tests. They move to the next grade if they pass. This system was built for the industrial age, when factories needed workers who could follow orders and repeat tasks. But the world has changed. The skills that factories needed are no longer the skills that life and work require. Many people now argue that education must change too. The first change they call for is in what we teach. In the past, knowing many facts was the mark of an educated person. Today, any fact can be found in seconds on a phone. What matters more is knowing what to do with facts. Students need to learn how to think, how to ask good questions, how to solve problems they have never seen before, and how to tell true information from false. The second change is in how we teach. Lectures have their place, but they should not be the only tool. Students learn best when they are active. They should build things, debate each other, work in teams, and create projects. They should make mistakes and learn from them, rather than only fear being wrong on a test. The third change is in how we measure success. A single test at the end of the year tells us little. It rewards those who are good at tests, not always those who understand deeply or who are creative. Some schools now use portfolios, where students collect their best work over time. Others assess students through real projects that solve real problems. The fourth change is in who gets a good education. In many countries, rich children get better schools and better teachers. Poor children are left behind. A just society must make sure every child, no matter how much money their family has, gets a chance to learn well. These changes are not easy. Teachers need new training. Parents must accept new ways. Governments must spend money. Some people fear that change will make things worse. But doing nothing is also a choice, and it is a dangerous one. The world will not wait for schools to catch up. Children grow up quickly. If we do not prepare them for the world they will actually live in, we fail them. Education should not be a factory. It should be a garden, where each child grows in their own way, with care, with challenge, and with joy. The goal is not to produce identical workers. It is to grow thoughtful, kind, and capable human beings.
articles.textCn: 今天的大多数学校看起来仍然很像一百年前的学校。孩子们坐成一排。他们听前面的老师讲课。他们记忆事实。他们参加考试。如果通过就升到下一年级。这个系统是为工业时代建造的，当时工厂需要能服从命令、重复任务的工人。但世界已经变了。工厂需要的技能不再是生活和工作所需的技能。许多人现在主张教育也必须改变。他们呼吁的第一个改变是我们教什么。过去，知道很多事实是受过教育的人的标志。今天，任何事实都能在几秒钟内用手机找到。更重要的是知道如何处理事实。学生需要学习如何思考、如何提出好问题、如何解决从未见过的问题，以及如何分辨真实和虚假的信息。第二个改变是我们如何教。讲授有它的位置，但不应该是唯一的工具。学生在活跃时学得最好。他们应该动手建造东西、互相辩论、团队合作、创建项目。他们应该犯错并从中学习，而不是只害怕考试答错。第三个改变是我们如何衡量成功。年底的一次考试告诉我们的很少。它奖励擅长考试的人，不总是深入理解或有创造力的人。一些学校现在使用作品集，让学生随时间收集最好的作品。另一些通过解决真实问题的真实项目来评估学生。第四个改变是谁能获得良好的教育。在许多国家，富家孩子得到更好的学校和更好的老师。穷家孩子被落下。一个公正的社会必须确保每个孩子，无论家里有多少钱，都有机会好好学习。这些改变不容易。教师需要新培训。父母必须接受新方式。政府必须花钱。有些人担心改变会让事情更糟。但什么都不做也是一种选择，而且是一种危险的选择。世界不会等待学校跟上。孩子们长得很快。如果我们不为他们将真正生活的世界做准备，我们就辜负了他们。教育不应该是一个工厂。它应该是一个花园，每个孩子以自己的方式成长，有关爱、有挑战、有快乐。目标不是生产一模一样的工人。而是培养有思想、善良、有能力的人。

articles.title: Mental Health in Modern Life
articles.titleCn: 现代生活中的心理健康
articles.text: For a long time, people did not talk about mental health. If someone felt sad for no clear reason, or could not stop worrying, or was afraid to leave the house, others often said they were just weak. They were told to be strong and forget about it. Today, we understand that mental health is just as real and important as physical health. The mind can be sick, just as the body can be sick, and both need care. Modern life brings many pressures. Young people worry about school, exams, and what others think of them. Adults worry about money, jobs, and raising children. Old people may feel lonely and useless. Social media adds a new kind of pressure. People see the best moments of others' lives and compare them to their own worst moments. They feel they are not good enough, not pretty enough, not successful enough. This quiet comparison slowly hurts the mind. The good news is that more people now understand that it is okay to ask for help. Seeing a counselor or a doctor for mental health is no longer strange in many countries. Schools have counselors. Workplaces offer support. Friends and families are learning to listen without judging. Still, there is much work to do. Many people still hide their pain because they feel ashamed. In some cultures, mental illness is seen as a family shame. This silence must end. Silence does not heal. It makes wounds deeper. There are also simple things each of us can do to protect our mental health. We can sleep enough, since tired minds are weak minds. We can move our bodies, since exercise lifts the mood. We can spend time with people who make us feel safe. We can spend less time on screens and more time in nature. We can learn to notice our own thoughts, and to question the cruel things we sometimes tell ourselves. We can also learn to be kind to others, because we never know what battle someone else is fighting. Mental health is not a personal weakness. It is a human condition. Everyone struggles at times. The strongest thing a person can do is not to hide their pain, but to face it, understand it, and seek help when needed. A society that cares for the mind as well as the body is a healthier, kinder, and stronger society.
articles.textCn: 很长一段时间，人们不谈论心理健康。如果有人没有明确原因地感到悲伤，或无法停止担忧，或害怕离开家，别人常说他只是脆弱。他们被告知要坚强，忘记它。今天，我们明白心理健康和身体健康一样真实和重要。心灵会生病，就像身体会生病，两者都需要照顾。现代生活带来很多压力。年轻人担心学校、考试和别人的看法。成年人担心金钱、工作和养育孩子。老人可能感到孤独和没用。社交媒体增加了新的压力。人们看到别人生活中最好的时刻，与自己最差的时刻比较。他们觉得自己不够好、不够漂亮、不够成功。这种悄悄的比较慢慢伤害心灵。好消息是，越来越多的人现在明白寻求帮助是正常的。在很多国家，因为心理健康看咨询师或医生不再奇怪。学校有咨询师。工作场所提供支持。朋友和家人正在学会不带评判地倾听。然而，还有很多工作要做。许多人仍因羞耻而隐藏痛苦。在一些文化中，心理疾病被视为家庭的耻辱。这种沉默必须结束。沉默不能治愈。它让伤口更深。也有一些简单的事我们每个人可以做来保护心理健康。我们可以睡足够，因为疲惫的心灵是脆弱的心灵。我们可以运动身体，因为锻炼能提升情绪。我们可以和让我们感到安全的人在一起。我们可以少看屏幕，多亲近自然。我们可以学会注意自己的想法，质疑有时我们对自己说的残酷的话。我们也可以学会善待他人，因为我们永远不知道别人在打什么仗。心理健康不是个人弱点。它是人类状况。每个人有时都会挣扎。一个人能做的最坚强的事不是隐藏痛苦，而是面对它，理解它，并在需要时寻求帮助。一个既关心心灵也关心身体的社会，是更健康、更善良、更强大的社会。

articles.title: Consumer Culture and Its Costs
articles.text: We live in an age of buying. Advertisements follow us on every screen. Shops are open day and night online. New things arrive every week, and old things are thrown away before they are broken. Many people feel that this endless buying makes them happy. But a closer look shows that consumer culture brings both pleasure and deep costs. On one hand, buying things can bring real joy. A new phone, a warm coat, or a good book can make life easier and more pleasant. Trade also gives jobs to millions of people, from factory workers to shop owners to delivery drivers. When people buy, the economy grows, and some of that growth can be used for schools, hospitals, and roads. On the other hand, the constant push to buy more has dark sides. First, it creates debt. Many young people buy things they cannot afford, using credit cards or loans. They spend years paying back money for things that lose value quickly. Second, it damages the planet. Every product takes energy, water, and materials to make. When we throw things away, they fill the earth and the sea with waste. The earth cannot keep up with our hunger for new things. Third, consumer culture can harm the mind. When happiness is tied to buying, people feel empty when they are not buying. They compare what they have with what others have, and they always feel they have too little. Advertisements teach us that we are not enough unless we buy this or that. This is a lie that slowly drains the soul. Fourth, consumer culture hides unfairness. The people who make our phones and clothes often work long hours for very little pay, in poor and sometimes dangerous conditions. When we buy cheap things, we often do not see the human cost behind the low price. What can we do? We do not need to stop buying altogether. That is neither possible nor wise. But we can buy less, choose things that last, and repair instead of replacing. We can ask where our things come from and who made them. We can find joy in things that money cannot buy, such as friendship, nature, art, and learning. True wealth is not having many things. It is needing few things and finding deep meaning in the life we have. A society that measures success only by how much it buys will always feel poor. A society that values care, creativity, and connection can feel rich with far less.
articles.textCn: 我们生活在一个购买的时代。广告在每个屏幕上跟着我们。网店日夜开放。每周都有新东西到货，旧东西在坏掉之前就被扔掉。许多人觉得这种无尽的购买让他们快乐。但仔细看，消费文化既带来快乐也带来深层代价。一方面，买东西能带来真正的快乐。一部新手机、一件暖和的外套、一本好书能让生活更轻松、更愉快。贸易也给了数百万人工作，从工厂工人到店主到快递员。人们购买时，经济增长，其中一部分增长可以用于学校、医院和道路。另一方面，不断推动买更多有阴暗面。首先，它造成债务。许多年轻人用信用卡或贷款买他们负担不起的东西。他们花好几年为快速贬值的东西还钱。其次，它损害地球。每个产品都需要能源、水和材料来制造。当我们扔掉东西时，它们用废物填满土地和海洋。地球跟不上我们对新事物的渴望。第三，消费文化会伤害心灵。当快乐与购买绑在一起时，人们在不买的时候感到空虚。他们比较自己拥有的和别人拥有的，总觉得拥有的太少。广告教我们，除非买这个那个，否则我们不够好。这是一个慢慢消耗灵魂的谎言。第四，消费文化掩盖了不公。制造我们手机和衣服的人往往工作很长时间，工资很少，条件差，有时危险。我们买便宜东西时，往往看不到低价背后的人的代价。我们能做什么？我们不需要完全停止购买。那既不可能也不明智。但我们可以少买，选择耐用的东西，修理而不是替换。我们可以问我们的东西从哪来、谁制造的。我们可以在金钱买不到的东西中找到快乐，如友谊、自然、艺术和学习。真正的财富不是拥有很多东西。它是需要很少的东西，并在我们拥有的生活中找到深层意义。一个只以购买多少衡量成功的社会，总会感到贫穷。一个重视关爱、创造力和联系的社会，可以用少得多的东西感到富有。

articles.title: Technology: A Double-Edged Sword
articles.text: Technology has changed the world more in one hundred years than all the centuries before. We can now talk to people on the other side of the earth in seconds. We can cure diseases that once killed millions. We can grow more food, build taller cities, and travel faster than our grandparents could dream. Technology has given us power that once belonged only to gods in old stories. But every power cuts both ways. The same technology that connects us also divides us. Phones let us talk to friends far away, but they also keep us from the people sitting next to us. We can share ideas with the whole world, but we can also spread lies and hate at the same speed. Social media was meant to bring us together, yet studies show that many people feel more lonely than ever. The internet gives us access to all human knowledge, yet it also floods us with false information, distractions, and noise. Many children now spend more time looking at screens than at the faces of their friends. Their ability to focus is growing weaker. Their anxiety is growing stronger. The same medical science that saves lives also creates new weapons that can end lives in vast numbers. The same chemistry that feeds the world also pollutes the rivers and the air. The same engines that let us travel the world also warm the planet and melt the ice. Technology itself is not good or evil. It is a tool. A knife can cut food or cut a person. A fire can warm a home or burn it down. The tool does not choose. The human hand that holds it does. The danger we face today is not that technology is too weak, but that our wisdom has not grown as fast as our power. We can do more than ever, but we are not always sure what we should do. We invent first and ask questions later. We build machines and then struggle to control them. The question for our age is not whether to use technology. We cannot give it up, and we should not try. The real question is how to use it wisely. This means we must teach not only skills but also values. We must teach children not only how to build things, but also when not to build them, and how to think about the effects of what they build. We must make rules that protect people without stopping useful progress. We must slow down enough to ask hard questions before we release new powers into the world. Above all, we must remember that technology should serve human beings, not the other way around. When a tool begins to use the user, something has gone wrong. The goal of technology should not be to do more things faster. It should be to help us live better, deeper, and more human lives. If we keep this goal in mind, technology can remain what it should be: a servant, not a master.
articles.textCn: 科技在一百年里改变世界，比之前所有世纪加起来还多。我们现在几秒钟内就能和地球另一边的人通话。我们能治愈曾经杀死数百万人的疾病。我们能种出更多粮食，建造更高的城市，比祖父母梦想的更快地旅行。科技给了我们曾经只属于古老故事中神灵的力量。但每种力量都有两面。连接我们的科技也在分裂我们。手机让我们和远方的朋友交谈，但也让我们忽略了身边的人。我们能向全世界分享想法，但也能以同样速度传播谎言和仇恨。社交媒体本是为了让我们在一起，但研究表明许多人感到前所未有的孤独。互联网让我们接触到所有人类知识，但也用虚假信息、干扰和噪音淹没我们。许多孩子现在看屏幕的时间比看朋友的脸还多。他们专注的能力在变弱。焦虑在变强。拯救生命的医学也制造了能大规模结束生命的新武器。喂养世界的化学也污染了河流和空气。让我们环游世界的引擎也在使地球变暖、融化冰川。科技本身不是善也不是恶。它是工具。刀可以切食物也可以伤人。火可以温暖房屋也可以烧毁它。工具不做选择。握住它的人做。我们今天面临的危险不是科技太弱，而是我们的智慧没有跟上我们的力量增长。我们能做的比以往都多，但不总是确定该做什么。我们先发明再提问。我们制造机器然后挣扎着控制它们。我们这个时代的问题不是是否使用科技。我们无法放弃它，也不应该尝试。真正的问题是如何明智地使用它。这意味着我们不仅要教技能，还要教价值观。我们不仅要教孩子如何建造东西，还要教他们何时不该建造，以及如何思考所建造之物的影响。我们必须制定保护人民而不阻碍有用进步的规则。我们必须放慢脚步，在向世界释放新力量之前提出难题。最重要的是，我们必须记住科技应该服务于人类，而不是相反。当工具开始使用使用者时，出了问题。科技的目标不应该是更快地做更多事。它应该是帮助我们过上更好、更深、更有人性的生活。如果我们记住这个目标，科技可以保持它应有的样子：仆人，而非主人。

articles.title: Globalization: Promise and Peril
articles.text: Globalization is the word we use for the growing connection between countries. Goods, money, people, and ideas now move across borders faster than ever before. A phone designed in one country may be built in another with parts from a dozen more, and sold in every nation on earth. A disease that begins in one city can reach every continent in days. A song made in one language can be sung by young people around the world. This growing connection has brought great gains. Millions of people have been lifted out of poverty as factories moved to countries where labor was cheaper. Goods that were once rare and costly are now common and cheap. Students can learn from the best teachers anywhere. Scientists in different countries work together on problems no single nation could solve alone. Cultures meet and mix, and from this meeting new art, new food, and new ideas are born. But globalization also brings problems that we cannot ignore. The first problem is unfairness. While some grew rich from global trade, others lost their jobs when factories moved away. Workers in rich countries found that their pay could not compete with workers in poor countries. The gap between those who benefit and those who suffer has grown wider. The second problem is the loss of local culture. When the whole world watches the same films, eats the same food, and listens to the same music, local languages and traditions begin to fade. A language dies every two weeks somewhere on earth. When a language dies, a way of seeing the world dies with it. The third problem is shared danger. Because we are so connected, a crisis in one place now touches everyone. A disease, a war, or a financial crash in one country can throw millions of people out of work on the other side of the world. We have built a system in which we all depend on each other, but we have not yet built the rules to manage that dependence fairly. The fourth problem is environmental. Global trade means goods travel long distances, burning fuel and releasing gases. The wealth that globalization creates often comes at the cost of the planet that sustains us. What should we do? We cannot close our borders and return to the past. The world is too connected now, and there are real benefits in that connection. But we must make globalization fairer. We must protect workers, not just profits. We must treasure local cultures, not erase them. We must build global rules for global problems, from disease to climate to finance. And we must remember that the goal of trade is not trade itself, but better lives for human beings. A connected world can be a richer, kinder, wiser world. But only if we guide it with care. Left alone, it will serve the strong and leave the weak behind. Guided well, it can lift everyone.
articles.textCn: 全球化是我们用来描述国家之间日益增长的联系的词。商品、金钱、人员和思想现在以前所未有的速度跨越国界。在一个国家设计的手机可能在另一个国家制造，零件来自十几个国家，然后在全球每个国家销售。一个城市开始的疾病几天内就能到达每个大陆。一种语言创作的歌曲可以被世界各地的年轻人传唱。这种日益增长的联系带来了巨大的收益。随着工厂搬到劳动力更便宜的国家，数百万人摆脱了贫困。曾经稀有昂贵的商品现在变得普通和便宜。学生可以向任何地方最好的老师学习。不同国家的科学家共同研究任何单一国家无法解决的问题。文化相遇和混合，从这种相遇中诞生了新的艺术、新的食物和新的思想。但全球化也带来了我们不能忽视的问题。第一个问题是不公平。一些人从全球贸易中致富，而另一些人在工厂搬走时失去了工作。富裕国家的工人发现自己的工资无法与贫穷国家的工人竞争。受益者和受害者之间的差距越来越大。第二个问题是本土文化的流失。当全世界看同样的电影、吃同样的食物、听同样的音乐时，当地语言和传统开始消退。地球上每两周就有一种语言消亡。一种语言消亡时，一种看世界的方式也随之消亡。第三个问题是共同危险。因为我们如此相连，一个地方的危机现在影响每个人。一个国家的疾病、战争或金融崩溃可以让世界另一端的数百万人失业。我们建立了一个相互依赖的系统，但还没有建立公平管理这种依赖的规则。第四个问题是环境问题。全球贸易意味着商品长途运输，燃烧燃料，释放气体。全球化创造的财富往往以维持我们的地球为代价。我们应该做什么？我们不能关闭边界回到过去。世界现在已经太相连了，这种联系有真正的好处。但我们必须让全球化更公平。我们必须保护工人，而不仅仅是利润。我们必须珍视本土文化，而不是抹去它们。我们必须为从疾病到气候到金融的全球问题建立全球规则。我们必须记住贸易的目的不是贸易本身，而是人类更好的生活。一个相连的世界可以是一个更富有、更善良、更智慧的世界。但只有我们用心引导它。放任不管，它将服务于强者，抛下弱者。引导得当，它可以提升每个人。

articles.title: The Philosophy of Time
articles.text: Time is one of the most mysterious aspects of our existence. We all experience it, yet we struggle to define it. Saint Augustine famously said, 'I know what time is if no one asks me, but if I am asked, I cannot explain it.' Physicists view time as a dimension, like space. Einstein's theory of relativity showed that time is not absolute. It can slow down or speed up depending on your speed and gravity. This is not just theory. GPS satellites have to account for time dilation, or they would be inaccurate. But philosophers see time differently. Some argue that the past, present, and future all exist simultaneously. This is the 'block universe' theory. Others argue that only the present exists. The past is a memory. The future is an expectation. Psychologists study how we perceive time. Time seems to speed up as we age. Childhood summers felt endless. Adult years fly by. One theory is that we process time relative to our memories. When we are young, everything is new. We form many memories. Time feels long. As we age, fewer things are new. We form fewer memories. Time feels short. This explains why new experiences make time feel longer. Cultures also view time differently. Some cultures are 'monochronic.' Time is linear. Schedules matter. Punctuality is important. Other cultures are 'polychronic.' Time is flexible. Relationships matter more than schedules. Our relationship with time affects our happiness. Many of us live in the past, regretting things we cannot change. Or we live in the future, worrying about things that may never happen. We miss the present. The present is the only time we truly have. Mindfulness practices teach us to be present. To focus on the 'now.' This can reduce anxiety and increase happiness. Time is also related to mortality. Knowing our time is limited makes each moment precious. It motivates us to use our time well. The philosophy of time asks big questions. What is time? How does it flow? Does the past exist? Is the future determined? These questions may never be fully answered. But asking them enriches our lives.

articles.title: The Story of the Universe
articles.text: The universe is 13.8 billion years old. It began with the Big Bang. Before the Big Bang, there was no space, no time—nothing. Then, in an instant, everything began. Space expanded. Time started. Energy filled the cosmos. In the first second, the universe was incredibly hot and dense. As it expanded, it cooled. After 380,000 years, atoms formed. The first atoms were hydrogen and helium. Gravity pulled them together. They formed stars. The first stars were huge. They burned hot and fast. They exploded as supernovae, creating heavier elements. Carbon, oxygen, iron—the elements of life. The explosions scattered these elements across space. New stars formed. Some had planets. Our sun formed 4.6 billion years ago. Earth was one of its planets. Earth was special. It was in the 'habitable zone.' Water could exist as a liquid. Liquid water is essential for life. Life appeared on Earth 3.8 billion years ago. No one knows exactly how. Simple molecules combined. They formed more complex molecules. They learned to copy themselves. This was the beginning of life. For billions of years, life stayed simple. Then, 540 million years ago, the Cambrian Explosion happened. Life exploded into complexity. Some had shells. Some had eyes. Life moved onto land. Plants, insects, amphibians, reptiles. Dinosaurs ruled for 180 million years. Then, 66 million years ago, an asteroid hit Earth. The dinosaurs died. Small mammals survived. One line of mammals evolved into primates. Primates evolved into humans. Humans appeared 300,000 years ago. We were not the strongest or fastest. But we were smart. We could make tools. We could speak. We could cooperate. We spread across the Earth. We learned to farm. We built cities. We invented writing. We explored the world. We discovered science. We went to the moon. We built machines that think. We are made of star dust. We are the universe, thinking about itself. The universe became aware of itself, through us. This is the story of the universe. It is our story. And it is still being written.

articles.title: The Psychology of Money
articles.text: Money affects our psychology in profound ways. It is not just a medium of exchange. It is a symbol. It represents value, status, security, freedom, and power. Psychologists have studied money for decades. They have found some surprising things. First, money can change our behavior. Studies have shown that just thinking about money makes people more independent. They prefer to work alone. They become less helpful. Money seems to activate a self-sufficient mindset. This can be good for productivity but bad for relationships. Second, money affects our perception of time. People who feel poor perceive time as moving faster. They feel they have less time. People who feel rich perceive time as moving slower. This affects decision-making. Third, money affects our morality. Studies have shown that wealthier people are more likely to cheat, lie, or break rules. This is not because rich people are bad. It is because wealth changes our psychology. It gives a sense of independence. It can also create a sense of superiority. Fourth, money affects our happiness. Money buys happiness up to a point. Once basic needs are met, more money does not bring more happiness. But the perception of wealth matters. People who feel they have more than their peers are happier. Comparison is the thief of joy. Fifth, money affects our relationships. Money is one of the biggest sources of conflict in marriages. Couples with different spending habits are more likely to divorce. Money also affects friendships. Borrowing money can damage a friendship. Sixth, money affects our identity. Many people define themselves by their wealth. This can be destructive. Money is a tool, not an identity. Seventh, money affects our stress. Financial stress is one of the biggest sources of anxiety. This stress affects health, relationships, and work. The healthy relationship with money? See money as a tool, not an end. Define enough. Don't compare yourself to others. Save. Give. Be honest. Learn. Money is not the root of all evil. But it is not the source of all happiness either. It is just a tool. Use it well.
